sk.recipe.line: {name}: one recipe of 400, {d} from today's computer, {status}.
sk.say.hello: This is today's computer. Open a rung to change it, or scroll out to see every attempt.
sk.say.yours: Yours now. Everything above it is made of it.
sk.say.broken: This switch never turns off. Nothing above it can be built.
sk.say.mended: It switches again, and the machine above it is back.
sk.say.newOne: A new recipe starts far behind: {v} of today's computer {need}. Once polished it could reach {could}.
sk.say.today: Today's computer again: level with itself in every need.
sk.say.year: Year {y}: {n} attempts into {dirs}. It stands at {v} of today's computer {need}.
sk.say.win: Year {y}: it beats today's computer {need}. Others join a winner: {p} people now.
sk.say.aim: It cannot serve that need ({what}). It now aims where it could do best: {need}.
sk.say.stone: Your switch spends less than silicon. Devices start further along: a stepping stone.
sk.say.first: You are the first to try this recipe.
sk.here.dig: Every 1 above starts here, as electrons crossing a gap of {eg} eV. Too small a gap and the switch can never turn off.
sk.here.digFork: Above this rung everything is still ones and zeros. Here a value is {what}.
sk.here.perfectOff: Perfect on paper, and it leaks in the world: with no gap it never turns off.
sk.here.physicsNew: A new way to switch lets physics do some of the work: steeper than the 60 mV line, at a price in speed.
sk.here.physicsLow: Close to {v} V you are fighting the spread of the copies to keep every 1 a 1.
sk.here.physicsFork: This carrier lets physical law do the sum itself. The price is on the plate: answers are no longer exact.
sk.here.moore: A new shape or material is what the next generation would be made of. Look at what it does to the machine at the top.
sk.here.perfect: Your gates are right on paper. At {v} V, {p} copies is late or wrong, and a chip has billions.
sk.here.vnVote: Three adders and a vote: the whole is now more reliable than any one of them, for three times the energy.
sk.here.vn: {p} sums comes out wrong. Could copies and a vote fix it?
sk.here.sutton: Lookahead is a clever human design. Given enough computing, a search finds adders nobody drew.
sk.here.geoMem: With {n} registers the wires take {p}% of each read. Bigger memory sits further away.
sk.here.geo: {p}% of the energy goes to moving numbers, not computing. Where the memory sits decides it.
sk.here.trust: This core has about {n} thousand gates. Nobody can test every state; what does your trust rest on?
sk.here.line5: A five-stage pipeline is fixed when it is made. A fork that rewires itself would trade speed for change.
sk.here.lineFixed: Wired for one job, it spends far less and can never do another.
sk.here.lineLearns: Nothing here was told what to do. It was shown examples, and it keeps changing.
sk.here.eff: Each answer costs {x} times less than the lab's example. Cheaper answers usually mean many more are asked.
sk.here.copyErr: Errors from below now change answers. A brain lives with its noisy cells; a copyable mind needs every bit exact.
sk.here.copyBits: Fewer bits a weight, fewer joules. How far can a machine drift from exact and still be the same mind on every copy?
sk.here.copyLive: This mind is grown, not written. It cannot be copied to a second machine.
sk.note.carry: the carry ripples slice to slice
sk.note.regs: each bit is ten of your gates
sk.ctl.stones: Stepping stones on this rung: {n} of {of} won
sk.genome.head: Proposed for the open genome: not grown by the engine until a fact backs it and the lab adopts it
sk.card.stack: Each rung is made of the one below. Open one to build it; a mark is a question that bites where you built.
sk.card.read: How is a mind built from atoms?
sk.card.rungs: The rungs, from the mind down
sk.card.dead: Nothing here can be built: the switch below never turns off.
sk.do.atom: Choose the matter. Which one can still turn off?
sk.do.switch: Take the voltage down as far as the copies allow.
sk.do.gate: Build every gate from one kind, or from many?
sk.do.block: Trade speed, spares and memory in one block.
sk.do.chip: Cut each instruction into stages: does the clock win?
sk.do.machine: How many units before moving numbers costs more than computing?
sk.do.mind: Fewer bits a weight: how far before it forgets?
